title_en: The Ruling on a Man Suckling His Wife's Milk
body_ar:
هل يجوز للرجل أن يرتضع لبن زوجته؟

الجواب: لا ليس للرجل ارتضاع لبن زوجته ، لأن ذلك ليس من الاستمتاع وإنما يجوز له المتعة؛ أي الاستمتاع بما أحله الله منها، والإرضاع ليس من تلك المتعة، لكن مذهب الجمهور أنه لو ارتضع لبنها فإنه لا يحرمها ذلك عليه ولا يخرجها عن عصمته خلافا لأم المومنين عائشة رضي الله عنها ولبعض علماء السلف فإنهم يرون أن الكبير تنتشر محرميته بالرضاع واستدلوا بحديث سلمة بنت سهيل أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أمرها أن ترضع سالما مولى أبي حذيفة وهو كبير، ومذهب الجمهور قصر انتشار الحرمة بالرضاع على الحولين، لقول الله تعالى " والوالدات يرضعن أولادهن حولين كاملين"، ولقوله تعالى "وحمله وفصاله ثلاثون شهرا، ولقوله تعالى " وفصاله في عامين".

وحديث سهلة يجاب عنه بأنه حالة خاصة لأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إنما أذن لها في إرضاع من كانت قد تبنته في الجاهلية ولا تبني بعد ذلك فإن التبني أبطله الإسلام بعد نزول آية سورة الأحزاب فلم يعد الإنسان ممكنا من تبني الغير بل يجب نسبته إلى أبيه كما قال الله تعالى " أدعوهم لآبائهم هو أقسط عند الله".

وهذه المرأة كانت تبنت سالما مدة طويلة فأصبحت بمثابة أمه فلذلك أذن لها في إرضاعه واليوم لا توجد امرأة قد تبنت رجلا على وجه شرعي فالتبني ليس جائزا.
body_en:
Is it permissible for a man to suckle his wife's milk?

The answer: No. It is not for a man to suckle his wife's milk, because that is not part of conjugal enjoyment. What is permissible to him is enjoyment (mutʿah) — that is, enjoyment of what God has made lawful to him from her — and suckling is not part of that enjoyment. But the position of the majority is that if he did suckle her milk, that does not make her forbidden to him and does not remove her from his marriage bond. This is contrary to the Mother of the Believers ʿA'isha, God be pleased with her, and to some of the scholars of the early generations, who hold that the milk relationship (raḍāʿ) does take effect in the case of an adult. They adduced as evidence the hadith of Salamah bint Suhayl, that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, commanded her to suckle Salim, the freedman of Abu Hudhayfah, when he was an adult. The position of the majority is to confine the taking effect of the prohibition through the milk relationship to the first two years, on the basis of the words of God, exalted: 'And mothers suckle their children two complete years'; and His words, exalted: 'And his bearing and his weaning are thirty months'; and His words, exalted: 'And his weaning is within two years.'

As for the hadith of Sahlah, the answer given to it is that it was a special case, because the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, gave her permission only to suckle one whom she had adopted in the age before Islam, and there is no adoption after that; for Islam abolished adoption after the verse of Sūrat al-Aḥzāb came down, so that a person is no longer able to adopt another, but rather ascribing him to his own father is obligatory, as God, exalted, said: 'Call them by their fathers' names; that is more equitable in the sight of God.'

This woman had adopted Salim for a long period, so that she had become as his mother, and for that reason he gave her permission to suckle him. Today there is no woman who has adopted a man in a manner recognised by the law, for adoption is not permissible.

flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT. The record names the Companion first as Salamah bint Suhayl and then, two lines later, as Sahlah — of the same hadith. The second form is the one attested in the collections (Sahlah bint Suhayl, wife of Abu Hudhayfah). The first is most probably a transcription slip. Both forms are preserved in body_ar and in the English per the house rule against silently fixing the source; the discrepancy is flagged rather than resolved.

flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW. This record is on one of the most easily sensationalised questions in the fiqh literature, and every clause of it matters. Note what the Sheikh actually holds and what he only reports. He rules that a man may not suckle his wife. He then reports, and does not adopt, the majority position that doing so would not dissolve the marriage. He then reports, and does not adopt, the minority position of ʿA'isha and some early scholars that adult suckling does create the impediment — and he goes on to give the majority's answer to their evidence, and to close off its application today by noting that adoption no longer exists in law. The attributions must stay visible and unambiguous in English, and no position here may be presented as his own beyond his opening 'No'. Translated faithfully; the publication decision belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office.

flags.arabic: لا ليس للرجل ارتضاع لبن زوجته
flags.context: the Sheikh's own ruling, the opening word of the answer
options: render literally as 'it is not for a man to …', using no five-rulings term
flags.note: The Sheikh states his ruling without using any of the five ruling terms: he says laysa li-l-rajul, 'it is not for a man', and grounds it in the scope of lawful conjugal enjoyment. Supplying ḥarām would strengthen the ruling beyond what he said, and makrūh would weaken it. Neither has been supplied.

Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

The three Qur'anic citations are given in the source between straight double quotation marks rather than the curly braces used elsewhere in the corpus, and without references. House style reserves curly braces for Qur'an; the source's own quotation marks have been kept in body_ar and the English uses single quotation marks to match the source's presentation rather than assert a Qur'anic frame the source did not use. The wordings match Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:233, Sūrat al-Aḥqāf 46:15, Sūrat Luqmān 31:14 and Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:5.
'Enjoyment' renders mutʿah in its sense of lawful conjugal enjoyment; this is not the mutʿah of temporary marriage, and the English must not be read that way.
The source spells أم المومنين for أم المؤمنين; preserved in body_ar.
